findings.title: Error-focused query detection is a substring match that misfires on negations and near-matches
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query does `"event.type:error" in query`, so any query containing that substring returns True — including a negated `!event.type:error` (which queries transactions/other event types) or unrelated tokens containing the substring. In those cases count() is replaced with sum(sample_weight) over non-error rows, where sample_weight is not populated, producing wrong or null counts. The check should parse the query filter (e.g. via EventSearch/parse_query) and verify event.type:error is an actual positive filter.

findings.title: 60s eligibility cache is never invalidated and causes stale/incorrect allowlist decisions
findings.body: The eligibility result is cached for 60 seconds keyed only by org + project ids, but invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called anywhere in the codebase, and the option value read at line 58 is mocked in tests anyway. When an operator adds or removes a project from `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`, existing cached entries keep serving the old decision for up to 60s — and since the cached True result also skips nothing dataset-specific (dataset/request are still checked, but the project allowlist decision is stale), counts can silently use (or skip) upsampling incorrectly. Worse, the cache makes the endpoint test suite order-dependent (see test gap finding).

findings.title: Upsampling decision uses the outer `dataset` closure instead of `scoped_dataset` and the request query instead of the actual query
findings.body: Inside _get_event_stats, is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects is called with the outer `dataset` variable, not the `scoped_dataset` argument that will actually execute the query. In the dashboard discover-split path, _get_event_stats is invoked with `discover` as scoped_dataset (and with modified queries like `... AND !event.type:transaction`), but the eligibility check still evaluates the original dataset and the original request.GET query string. This means split queries against discover can be mis-classified (e.g. the errors-only split query will only be upsampled if the user's original query contained 'event.type:error', and a transaction-like split could get the transform if the original dataset was errors). The check must use scoped_dataset and the `query` argument actually being executed.

findings.title: upsampled_count registered only on the discover dataset, but the transform is also applied for the errors dataset
findings.body: _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns True unconditionally when dataset == sentry.snuba.errors, and the endpoint then rewrites count() to upsampled_count(). However the SnQLFunction `upsampled_count` is only added to the discover dataset's function_converter. If the errors dataset resolves functions through a different dataset/builder (which it does — errors uses its own dataset class), queries against the errors endpoint will fail with an unknown-function error whenever all queried projects are allowlisted, i.e. the feature breaks the errors dataset path entirely. The function must be registered on every dataset where the transform can be applied, or the errors dataset path must be verified/covered by tests.

findings.title: count() inside aliases or equations is silently not transformed, producing inconsistent upsampling
findings.body: transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only matches the exact string 'count()' (case/whitespace-insensitive). Columns like 'count() as total_events', count() used inside yAxis equations, or 'count()' embedded in other aggregate forms pass through unchanged, so a chart mixing 'count()' and 'count() as total' would show one upsampled and one raw series on the same chart. At minimum the alias form should be handled or the mismatch documented, and equations containing count() are a known gap.

findings.title: No handling of events lacking sample_weight in allowlisted projects
findings.body: The docstring asserts the schema guarantees sample_weight exists for all events in allowlisted projects, but the factory change in testutils/factories.py shows sample_rate is only set when contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate is present. Historical events ingested before the feature rolled out (or from SDKs without error sampling) have no sample_weight; sum(sample_weight) over those rows will yield null/0 rather than a count, undercounting errors dramatically. There is no fallback (e.g. coalesce(sample_weight, 1)) or date-boundary guard restricting the transform to post-rollout periods.

findings.title: Endpoint upsampling tests are order-dependent and will fail spuriously due to the shared 60s cache
findings.body: The tests mock options.get but not the cache. The first test (full allowlist) caches eligible=True under the key for org+sorted project ids; the subsequent 'partial allowlist' test runs with the same org and same project set, so it will read the cached True and expect count==1 while the code path actually upsamples to 10 — the assertion at 'Should use regular count()' would fail depending on test execution order. The tests must clear the cache between cases (or mock cache.get to return None); as written they prove the caching behavior is untested and the suite is flaky.

findings.title: Accidental submodule/placeholder file 'sentry-repo' committed
findings.body: The PR adds a one-line file `sentry-repo` containing 'Subproject commit a5d290...'. This looks like an accidentally created git submodule/gitlink entry pointing at the base commit, unrelated to the feature. It should be removed before merging.

findings.title: Allowlist membership check is O(n*m) on every cache miss
findings.body: `all(project_id in allowlist for project_id in project_ids)` performs a linear scan of the allowlist list for every project. With a large allowlist option and many projects this is quadratic-ish per request. Converting the allowlist to a set before the check is a trivial fix; also worth noting the option lookup is described as 'expensive' but options.get is an in-memory cached lookup, so the 60s cache adds staleness risk for little benefit.

findings.title: upsampled_count declares default_result_type 'number' though it emits toInt64
findings.body: The SnQLFunction wraps the aggregate in toInt64(...) but declares default_result_type="number" (float), while plain count() uses "integer". This can make downstream consumers (zerofill, response formatting, chart interpolation) treat the column as a float series and format/interpolate it differently from count(), an inconsistency for a function intended to be a drop-in replacement.
